draft.rationale: The new write loop swallows every write failure with an empty catch, so a partial or empty export is returned as success. A disk or permission fault reaches nobody.
save() now hides a failed write behind a comment-only catch and returns normally, so a caller cannot tell that the preferences were not persisted. The user assumes settings were stored.
A malformed row is parsed inside a comment-only catch, so a broken payload is counted as a skipped row instead of failing the import. The operator sees a successful import with missing contacts.
The library caller gets a count and no failure when a usage post fails; the log line is the only trace and the caller never learns that billing data was dropped. A log is not handling.
The edit wraps the webhook send in a catch that only logs and lets the loop continue, so the returned list silently omits a shipment whose notification never happened.
flush() used to propagate the append failure and now logs it and returns success, so audit entries are lost while the caller believes they are durable.

A failed flag read or a corrupt payload now returns the default flag set, which is indistinguishable from a successful read of flags that happen to be off. Operators see features vanish with no error.
A database failure now reads as an empty open-orders list, so the report and its total quietly show zero. The caller has no way to tell a fault from a genuine empty result.
A failed read of the required service config returns a hardcoded default config, so the service runs against the wrong endpoint and region with no signal that configuration was never loaded.

The validity check is replaced by `?? emptyCatalog`, so a corrupt catalog becomes an empty one and every lookup silently misses. The absent value is caused by a parse failure, not by an optional field.

A failed or empty database read is replaced by a hardcoded rate with `||`, so invoices are taxed at a stale figure instead of failing. The rate is absent because the read failed, not because it is optional.

A failed coupon lookup collapses into `?? 0`, so a customer with a valid code is charged full price and nobody sees the fault. The default parameter hides the failure rather than reporting an unusable coupon.
The edit drops the `ok` check and invents an order id, so a rejected save is reported to the customer as a placed order. The failure object is received and never inspected.
Rejections from Promise.allSettled are dropped: a failed transfer only shortens the receipt list and nothing surfaces which payouts failed. The caller reads the settlement as complete.
The catch-all wraps the failure in a typed domain error and rethrows it, so the caller still cannot proceed without noticing. Wrapping and rethrowing is the exception, not a swallow.

The catch converts the failure into a typed `{ ok: false }` outcome that the only caller checks, so the fault cannot be mistaken for success. Returning a failure the caller must handle is the exception.
The catch returns `Result.Err` with a gateway code, which the signature forces the caller to handle. A typed failure value is the exception, not a plausible normal result.
The catch is narrow: it returns undefined only for the expected ENOENT of an optional attachment and rethrows everything else. Expected absence by contract plus a narrow catch is the exception.

tryParseFilters has the documented try-parse contract of returning undefined for absent or invalid input, and the caller falls back to empty filters. Keeping a bad stored filter from breaking the page is the expected-absence exception.
The ignored rejection belongs to closing a handle after the bytes were already written, so it cannot change the caller's result. Best-effort cleanup of that kind is the exception.
Only a telemetry span export is swallowed, which cannot change the result of the measured work. Metrics emission failing harmlessly is the best-effort exception.
This is the request boundary: the catch logs the fault and answers 500, which the user and the operator both see. A boundary that turns the error into a visible outcome is the exception.
runRebuild is the job entry point: it logs the failure, sets a non-zero exit code and returns that code, so the run is visibly failed. A boundary that reports and signals the error is the exception.
The swallowed error sits in a test fixture loader. Test code is excluded from this rule.
The added catch is inside a spec helper, so the failure only affects a test run. Test code is excluded from this rule.

The log-only catch was already there; the edit only adds a sender accessor whose `??` covers an optional configured address. The pre-existing debt is untouched, so the edit neither introduces nor worsens a silent failure.

refresh() already returned an empty list on any fetch failure before this edit and still does; the edit only adds a count accessor whose `??` covers the normal not-yet-loaded state. Unchanged existing debt does not warrant a nudge.
The `.catch(() => [])` that turns an API failure into no renewals was already in the file and is untouched. The edit adds an unrelated predicate, so concern stays as it was and no nudge is due.
The edit makes save() rethrow after logging, so the failure now reaches the caller; the previous silent failure is resolved. Resolving a concern does not warrant a nudge.
The edit replaces `catch { return [] }` with a typed throw, so a failed line load no longer reads as a zero total. The previous silent failure is resolved, so no nudge is due.
The new catch adds context and rethrows the failure, so the caller still sees it. Nothing is hidden, so there is nothing to report.
The added code returns a typed check result and the wrapper throws on the failure branch, so the invalid-address outcome is checked and surfaced. It handles the failure rather than hiding it.
`return []` here is the honest answer for an empty input list in a pure in-memory filter; no operation can fail, so no failure is being hidden.
The `??` covers a trailing reference column that many bank exports omit, which is optional by format rather than absent because something failed. No fault is hidden.
The `.then` chain has no catch, so a rejection from the suggest service propagates to the caller unchanged. Nothing is converted or swallowed.
Every rejection from allSettled is collected and the batch throws when any conversion failed, so no failure is lost. This is the correct handling, not a silent one.
The added switch only maps a status to a display string and no operation can fail; there is no catch, fallback or failure value anywhere in the edit.
Both `??` fallbacks fill genuinely optional fields (no preferred name, no company) for a display string; no operation ran and failed. Nothing is hidden from the caller.
The edit only adds a pure geometry calculation; it neither handles nor suppresses any failure.
The `finally` only resets an in-flight flag; a rejection from list or upsert still propagates to the caller. No failure is caught, converted or ignored.
